# Codex native metadata paging

Authorized real CLI connection on 13 October 2026 exposed FRAME_LIMIT during MCP inventory. A separate bounded diagnostic retained only method names, byte sizes and row counts: initialize245B, account/read283B, model/list7880B, mcpServerStatus/list approximately1045593B across8servers—too close to the unchanged1048576B frame ceiling, with variable live tool inventories. No raw frames, auth/config files or provider credentials were retained.

Request at most4servers per MCP page and reject a response exceeding4. Frame/output/tool/count/timeouts and the existing8-page cap remain unchanged; all pages must complete before isolation. No partial inventory is used for native authority or a model turn. This tightens the effective discovery cap to32servers and fails closed above that cap; it does not omit unknown servers or silently truncate a catalogue. Native config files are not modified. The authorized real connection was rechecked successfully: HTTP200, acknowledged, ready subscription metadata and seven reported models, with isolation still pending and no thread. Evidence: `runtime/verification/native-cli-bootstrap-connect-MpZFLr/verification.json`. No inference or Studio commands are part of this proof.

The authorized native diagnostic also showed connection-level runtimeStatus:null for every server: runtime state is unavailable before a thread exists. Secret-free discovery may accept null ONLY for the fixed disabled, nonplugin Arcane entry with no tools and no discovery error. This does not verify isolation or grant anything. Final native credentials remain unbound; configured thread inventory still requires concrete connected Arcane plus disabled inherited servers before any turn/grant. The previous unconditional connection-level runtime requirement is not a native contract.
